previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for severe bilateral leg cramps and hyperglycemia with glucose up to 500. Labs revealed hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and acute-on-chronic kidney injury likely due to dehydration and uncontrolled diabetes exacerbated by prednisone. She was treated with IV fluids and albumin, which resolved her electrolyte abnormalities and myalgias. A diagnostic paracentesis showed mild ascites without infection. Her insulin regimen was optimized with a switch to 70/30 NPH-humalog 40 units in the morning and 20 units at bedtime, along with a sliding scale. She was instructed to report daily blood glucose values to her diabetologist. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with follow-up arranged.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PA AND LAT)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman s/p liver transplant with dyspnea  // rule out
pneumonia      rule out pneumonia

IMPRESSION: 

Compared to chest radiographs ___ through ___.

There are no new findings.  Small region of pleural parenchymal scarring at
the base the left lung is stable.  Heart size is top-normal.  No pulmonary
vascular abnormality or focal consolidation.  Mediastinum and hilar contours
are normal.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with cirrhosis s/p OLT w/recurrent cirrhosis
c/b worsening ascites.  // Please evaluate for SBP, please perform therapeutic
paracentesis

TECHNIQUE:  Paracentesis ___

FINDINGS: 

Limited grayscale ultrasound imaging of the abdomen demonstrated a small
amount of ascites. A suitable target in the deepest pocket in the right lower
quadrant was selected for paracentesis.

PROCEDURE:  The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed
with the patient and written informed consent was obtained.

A preprocedure time-out was performed discussing the planned procedure,
confirming the patient's identity with 3 identifiers, and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected and the skin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. 1% lidocaine was instilled
for local anesthesia.

A 5 ___ catheter was advanced into the largest fluid pocket in the right
lower quadrant and 0.9 L of cloudy, straw-colored fluid was removed. Fluid
samples were submitted to the laboratory for cell count, differential,
culture, and cytology.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication.
Estimated blood loss was minimal.

Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key components of the
procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful ultrasound-guided therapeutic and diagnostic
paracentesis with removal of 0.9 L cloudy, straw-colored ascitic fluid.
